syllabus: Structure follows the RCM Piano Syllabus, 2022 edition (rcmusic.com/syllabi)

lessons.title: Pentascales: C and G major
lessons.learn: A pentascale is the first five notes of a scale, up and down, ending with the tonic triad played as a chord. Play legato: join each note smoothly to the next.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Right hand 1 2 3 4 5, left hand 5 4 3 2 1 going up.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Pentascales: D major and A minor
lessons.learn: D major has two sharps (F♯ and C♯); in its pentascale you meet F♯. A minor uses only white keys, and its triad sounds darker than a major one.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Listen to the difference between the major and minor triads at the end.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Staccato pentascales
lessons.learn: The same pentascales played staccato: short and detached, bouncing off each key (the dots above or below the notes).
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Let the hand bounce lightly from the wrist; keep the fingers close to the keys.

lessons.title: Triad sequence in C major
lessons.learn: Build a triad (three notes a third apart) on every note of the C major scale, going up: first broken, one note at a time, then solid, all together.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Keep the same hand shape (1 3 5 in the right hand, 5 3 1 in the left) and move it up one key at a time.

lessons.title: Middle C and friends
lessons.learn: Find middle C (the C nearest the middle of the keyboard, just left of the two black keys) and play C, D and E with fingers 1, 2 and 3 of your right hand.
tips: Thumb = 1, pointer = 2, middle = 3, ring = 4, little finger = 5.
Curve your fingers as if holding a ball; play with the fingertips.
Keep your thumb resting on middle C between notes.

lessons.title: Au clair de la lune
lessons.learn: A French folk song with quarter, half and whole notes. Feel the long notes without rushing.
tips: Hold the half notes for two full beats.
Try Play along to feel the steady beat.

lessons.title: Five-finger position
lessons.learn: Put one finger on each key from C to G. This "C position" lets you play five notes without moving your hand.
tips: Each finger stays over its own key: C=1, D=2, E=3, F=4, G=5.
Let the 4th and 5th fingers play as clearly as the others; go slowly.

lessons.title: Left hand five fingers
lessons.learn: The left hand uses the same numbers, but its thumb is on the right. In C position below middle C: C=5, D=4, E=3, F=2, G=1.
tips: Read the bass clef: the line between the two dots is F.
Your left thumb sits on the G just below middle C.

lessons.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
lessons.learn: Your first song, all in C position. Notice the half notes (2 beats) and the whole note at the end (4 beats).
tips: Count "1 2 3 4" in every bar.
Hold half and whole notes for their full length.

lessons.title: Hot Cross Buns
lessons.learn: A left-hand song that introduces eighth notes: two of them fit in one beat.
tips: Say "1-and 2-and" for the eighth notes.
Keep the eighth notes even, like a ticking clock.

lessons.title: Lightly Row
lessons.learn: A cheerful German folk tune ("Hänschen klein") that stays in C position from start to finish.
tips: The melody often steps down; keep each finger over its own key.
In the middle part, play the repeated notes evenly.

lessons.title: Old MacDonald Had a Farm
lessons.learn: A song in F major. The thumb sits on C below F, and finger 3 plays F, so you skip the E.
tips: Right hand: C 1, D 2, F 3, G 4, A 5.
Hold the whole note for four full beats.

lessons.title: Ear tests
lessons.learn: Clap back a rhythm, tell whether a chord is major or minor, and play back a short melody on the first three notes of the scale.

lessons.title: Sight reading
lessons.learn: Tap a rhythm at sight, then play two four-note melodies: one in the right hand (treble clef), one in the left (bass clef). They move by step in one direction.

lessons.title: C major scale, right hand
lessons.learn: Play eight notes in a row by passing the thumb under: after E (finger 3), the thumb plays F. Coming down, finger 3 crosses over the thumb onto E.
tips: Move the thumb under early, while finger 3 plays.
Keep the wrist level; do not twist it.
Then try the eighth notes in bars 5-6.

lessons.title: C major scale, left hand
lessons.learn: For the left hand the crossing happens going up: after G (thumb), finger 3 crosses over onto A. Coming down, the thumb passes under after A.
tips: Fingering up: 5 4 3 2 1, 3 2 1.
Fingering down: 1 2 3, 1 2 3 4 5.

lessons.title: G major scale: your first sharp
lessons.learn: The key signature has one sharp (F♯), so every F is played on the black key just right of F. The fingering is the same as the C scale.
tips: Finger 4 plays F♯.
Look at the key signature at the start of every new piece.

lessons.title: C scale, hands together
lessons.learn: Both hands play the C scale together, an octave apart. The thumbs cross at different moments, which is the real challenge.
tips: Practise slowly with Wait for me.
Right thumb crosses on F; left finger 3 crosses on A going up.

lessons.title: Contrary motion scale
lessons.learn: The hands move in opposite directions, mirroring each other. Both use the same fingers at the same time, which makes it easier than the parallel scale.
tips: Both thumbs cross under at the same moment.
Listen for the hands to sound exactly together.

lessons.title: Pentascales: D, A and F major
lessons.learn: Pentascales in eighth notes. A major has F♯ and C♯ in its first five notes; F major has none (its B♭ is the 4th note of the scale, beyond the pentascale).
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Two notes per beat: count "1 and 2 and".
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Pentascales: E and D minor
lessons.learn: Minor pentascales in eighth notes, legato. Then try them staccato too.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
E minor has F♯; D minor uses only white keys in its first five notes.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: One-octave scales: C, G major and A minor
lessons.learn: Full one-octave scales hands separately, with the thumb passing under. A minor here is the natural minor (all white keys).
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Right hand 1 2 3 1 2 3 4 5; left hand 5 4 3 2 1 3 2 1.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Tonic triads: C, G major and A minor
lessons.learn: The tonic triad in root position, first inversion and second inversion, broken, going up and back down, ending with the solid chord.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Right hand fingering: root 1 3 5, first inversion 1 2 5, second inversion 1 3 5.
Left hand: root 5 3 1, first inversion 5 3 1, second inversion 5 2 1.

lessons.title: Veni Creator Spiritus (Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The Pentecost hymn in its chant melody (mode 7, Mixolydian): a flowing line over a small range, right hand alone.
tips: Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
Play legato, as if singing one long breath.
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Regina caeli (Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The Easter antiphon "Regina caeli, laetare, alleluia": a short chant line for the right hand, with the words under the notes.
tips: Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
Play legato, as if singing one long breath.
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
lessons.learn: The melody goes beyond five notes, so the right hand shifts: after the first C, finger 4 takes G and 5 takes A.
tips: Watch the finger numbers where the hand moves.
The left hand plays C, F and G; keep it in place with the thumb on C.

lessons.title: London Bridge
lessons.learn: The melody uses six notes, so the right hand sits one key higher than C position: thumb on D, little finger on A.
tips: The dotted quarter and eighth sound "long-short".
At the end the thumb moves down from D to C.

lessons.title: When the Saints Go Marching In
lessons.learn: Each phrase starts after a rest. Feel the rest on beat 1, then come in on beat 2.
tips: Count the rest out loud: "(1) 2 3 4".
The left hand holds whole notes: C, then G or F where the harmony changes.

lessons.title: Ode to Joy, hands together
lessons.learn: Play the melody with the right hand while the left hand holds long notes. Start with one hand at a time (choose Right or Left), then Both.
tips: Practise each hand alone first.
The left hand only changes at the start of each bar.
The dotted quarter is 1½ beats: "1 2-and".

lessons.title: Frère Jacques
lessons.learn: The famous round, with the left hand holding a drone (C and G together) underneath: your first steady accompaniment.
tips: The left hand just holds; let the right hand lead.
In bars 7–8 the right hand dips down to the G below middle C.

lessons.title: Jingle Bells
lessons.learn: The famous chorus, all in C position. Repeated notes need a light, bouncy touch.
tips: Keep finger 3 on E for the opening "jingle bells".
The left hand changes to F in bar 5 and G in bars 7–8.

lessons.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
lessons.learn: A round in 6/8 time: each bar has two big beats, each split into three. The "merrily" bar uses a stretched hand from C to the C above.
tips: Count "1-2-3 4-5-6" with the stress on 1 and 4.
In bar 5 the hand opens to an octave: C (5), G (3), E (2), C (1).

lessons.title: Minuet in F (attributed to Leopold Mozart)
lessons.learn: An elegant minuet in F major (one flat: B♭). Short, detached chords in the left hand answer the right-hand tune, which mixes slurred and staccato notes.
tips: The dots mean staccato: short and light. The slurs mean smooth.
The left hand plays two-note chords on beats 2 and 3, and rests on beat 1.
Every B is B♭ in this key, except where a natural sign says otherwise.
lessons.syl: Preparatory B · List A: Minuet in F Major, attr. L. Mozart (Notebook for Nannerl)

lessons.title: Ear tests
lessons.learn: Clap back a rhythm, tell major from minor, and play back a melody on the first three notes of a major or minor scale.

lessons.title: Sight reading
lessons.learn: Tap a rhythm at sight, then play a short melody shared between the hands in C position.

lessons.title: Two-octave scales: C, G and F major
lessons.learn: Two-octave scales hands separately. The thumb passes under twice on the way up. F major has B♭ and its own right-hand fingering: 1 2 3 4, 1 2 3, 1 2 3 4.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
All scales are legato.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Minor scales: A, E and D (natural and harmonic)
lessons.learn: Each minor key twice: first the natural minor, then the harmonic minor, which raises the 7th note (G♯ in A minor, D♯ in E minor, C♯ in D minor).
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Listen for the raised 7th: it pulls strongly back to the tonic.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Contrary motion, two octaves
lessons.learn: C major in contrary motion over two octaves, hands together: the hands move away from each other and back, using the same finger numbers at the same time.
tips: Both thumbs pass under at the same moment.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Chromatic scale from C
lessons.learn: Every key, black and white, for one octave. Black keys use finger 3, white keys the thumb, except where two white keys sit together (E–F, B–C), which use 1–2.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Keep the hand close to the black keys; the thumb and finger 3 do most of the work.

lessons.title: Tonic triads: C, G and F major (broken)
lessons.learn: Broken tonic triads through root position and both inversions, up and down, ending with the solid chord.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Keep the wrist level as the hand moves to each inversion.

lessons.title: Tonic triads: A, E and D minor (broken)
lessons.learn: The minor tonic triads, broken, through all inversions.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
The minor triad has a minor third (3 half steps) at the bottom.

lessons.title: Solid tonic triads: C, G, F, A, E and D
lessons.learn: The same triads played solid (all notes together), with a rest after each chord.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Press the three notes exactly together and release them together on the rest.

lessons.title: Veni Sancte Spiritus (Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The "Golden Sequence" of Pentecost in the Dorian mode: a long right-hand line, several notes to a syllable.
tips: Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
Play legato, as if singing one long breath.
lessons.license: Public domain music; edition CC BY 4.0, (c) 2019 Freshman Chorus of St. John's College of Annapolis, via the Choral Public Domain Library (cpdl.org)

lessons.title: Adoro te devote (Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The hymn of St Thomas Aquinas as a chant: a longer right-hand melody with the Latin words, in long bars of eight beats.
tips: Count in quarter notes; the bars are long (8 beats).
Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
Play legato, as if singing one long breath.
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Ave verum corpus (Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The Eucharistic hymn as a chant melody, for the right hand, with the Latin words under the notes.
tips: Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
Play legato, as if singing one long breath.
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Our Father (Gregorian chant, left hand)
lessons.learn: A chant in A major (three sharps) for the left hand alone, in the bass clef: a good way to read the lower staff.
tips: Three sharps: F♯, C♯ and G♯.
Left hand: the thumb (1) is on the highest note.
Chant has no strict beat: let the notes flow in a gentle, even pace.
lessons.license: Public domain music; edition freely distributable (Choral Public Domain Library, cpdl.org)

lessons.title: Three chords: C, F and G
lessons.learn: Most simple songs use three chords. Keep the right thumb on C: C chord = C E G (1 3 5), F chord = C F A (1 4 5), G chord = B D G (1 2 5).
tips: Press all chord notes at exactly the same time.
Move as few fingers as possible between chords.
The left hand plays the chord name: C, F or G.

lessons.title: Ode to Joy (piano for kids)
lessons.learn: Another easy setting of the Ode to Joy melody, for hands together.
tips: Practise each hand alone first.
Keep the left hand steady while the right hand sings.
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML arrangement from MuseScore.com

lessons.title: Ode to Joy (with left-hand chords)
lessons.learn: The famous melody again, with the left hand playing a whole note under each bar and chords in the last bar of each phrase. A good test of hands together.
tips: Left hand: C with the little finger, then G with the thumb, then E with finger 3.
The last bar of each section has a two- or three-note chord: press the notes together.
Get louder in the last line, then slow down at the end.

lessons.title: Ode to Joy with broken chords
lessons.learn: The left hand now plays its chord one note at a time (a broken chord), which makes the music flow. This kind of pattern is used in lots of classical pieces.
tips: Learn the left-hand pattern alone first: 5 1 3 1.
Keep the left hand quieter than the melody.

lessons.title: Greensleeves
lessons.learn: A minor-key melody in 3/4 with a pickup. Watch for the sharps (F♯ and G♯) that give it its old, haunting sound.
tips: The rhythm "long-short-long" (dotted quarter, eighth, quarter) repeats through the song.
Finger 3 crosses over the thumb in bar 8.

lessons.title: Away with Melancholy
lessons.learn: A cheerful tune from Mozart's The Magic Flute. It starts with a short pickup (two eighth notes), and the left hand plays steady half notes, then simple chords in the second half.
tips: Count "4 and" before the first note: the tune starts on the last beat of an empty bar.
The rests in bars 3, 5, 11 and 13 are part of the tune: wait for them.
In the second half the left hand plays two-note chords: press both notes together.

lessons.title: Happy Birthday
lessons.learn: In 3/4 time with a pickup: the song starts before the first full bar. It is in F major, so every B is played as B♭.
tips: Count "3 | 1 2 3": the two short opening notes come on beat 3.
In bar 5 the hand leaps up to the high C with finger 5.

lessons.title: Silent Night
lessons.learn: A gentle carol in 6/8 that moves around the keyboard. Look ahead to the finger number at each new phrase: the hand moves to a new position.
tips: Play smoothly, joining the notes (legato).
The left hand plays just C, F and G.

lessons.title: Aria in F (BWV Anh. 131)
lessons.learn: A flowing aria from the Anna Magdalena notebook, in F major. Both hands sing: the left hand answers the right in long, smooth lines, and in the second half it plays light staccato notes.
tips: Start with the pickup: one beat before the first full bar.
There is a B♮ in bars 6 and 7: the natural sign cancels the B♭.
Keep the phrase marks smooth and lift lightly at the end of each slur.
lessons.syl: Level 1 · Complete list: Aria in F Major, BWV Anh. 131

lessons.title: Chorale in C (BWV 514)
lessons.learn: A chorale-like piece in 3/4 where the two hands move as independent melodies. Listen for the little sixteenth-note ornaments in bars 3 and 11.
tips: Learn each hand separately: both have their own tune.
The two sixteenth notes take half of one beat together: "1 and-a".
Bar 6 has an F♯ in the left hand and bar 8 an F♮: watch the signs.
lessons.syl: Level 1 · Complete list: Chorale, BWV 514 (Notenbuch der Anna Magdalena Bach)

lessons.title: Minuet in C, Op. 38 No. 4
lessons.learn: A short classical minuet from Hässler's 50 Pieces for Beginners. The right hand sings; the left hand has long notes and little eighth-note turns. Look for the answering phrases: bars 1-4 and 9-12 are nearly the same.
tips: Learn each hand alone first, then together.
Bar 6 has a G♯ and bar 7 a C♯: watch the accidentals.
Play the last-bar chords together, then lift the hands for the final C.
Keep it light and graceful: one beat per quarter, a gentle lilt on beat 1.
lessons.syl: Level 1 · List A: Minuet in C Major, op. 38, no. 4 (Hässler)

lessons.title: Minuet in F, K. 2
lessons.learn: One of the first pieces Mozart wrote, at the age of five. A graceful minuet in F major (one flat, B♭).
tips: Play it lightly and with a gentle lilt on beat 1.
Every B is B♭ in this key.
lessons.syl: Level 1 · Complete list: Minuet in F Major, K 2 (W.A. Mozart)
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML arrangement from MuseScore.com

lessons.title: Andante in G minor
lessons.learn: A calm Baroque andante in G minor (two flats) in 2/4: a singing right hand over a steady left hand.
tips: Two flats: B♭ and E♭.
Keep the left hand quiet so the tune sings.
lessons.syl: Level 1 · List A: Andante in G Minor (Telemann)
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML from the Sao Mai Center for the Blind

lessons.title: Ear tests
lessons.learn: Clap back a rhythm, name minor and major thirds, tell major from minor, and play back a five-note melody.

lessons.title: Sight reading
lessons.learn: Tap a rhythm at sight, then play a four-bar melody shared between the hands in C, G, F major or A minor.

lessons.title: Two-octave scales: G, F and B♭ major
lessons.learn: B♭ major starts on a black key, so its fingering begins with finger 4 in the right hand and 3 in the left: the thumbs land on C and F.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
B♭ major, right hand: 4 1 2 3 1 2 3 4; left hand: 3 2 1 4 3 2 1 3.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Harmonic minor scales: E, D and G
lessons.learn: Harmonic minor raises the 7th note going up and down: D♯ in E minor, C♯ in D minor, F♯ in G minor.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Melodic minor scales: E, D and G
lessons.learn: Melodic minor raises the 6th and 7th notes going up and comes down as the natural minor.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.
Going up it sounds almost like major; coming down it is minor again.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Chromatic scale from G
lessons.learn: The chromatic scale starting on G. The same rule: black keys 3, white keys 1, and 1–2 where two white keys meet.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.

lessons.title: Tonic triads: G, F, B♭ major and E, D, G minor (broken)
lessons.learn: Broken tonic triads in the Level 2 keys, through all inversions.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.

lessons.title: Solid tonic triads: G, F, B♭ major and E, D, G minor
lessons.learn: The Level 2 tonic triads played solid with rests, up and down.
tips: Hands separately: the right hand plays first, then the left hand.

lessons.title: Canon (Pachelbel), simplified
lessons.learn: The famous Canon, in C major and in slow half notes. The left hand repeats the same eight-note bass line, the melody walks down above it.
tips: Going down, finger 3 crosses over the thumb.
Let each half note ring for its full two beats.

lessons.title: Little Waltz in A minor
lessons.learn: An original Romantic-style waltz. The left hand plays the classic waltz accompaniment: a low bass note on beat 1, a chord on beats 2 and 3.
tips: Make beat 1 of the left hand a little deeper; keep the chords on 2 and 3 light.
Shape the melody: grow toward bar 6 and relax at the end.
lessons.why: only eight bars of a simple oom-pah-pah waltz

lessons.title: Sanctus (Kyriale XVII, Gregorian chant)
lessons.learn: The Sanctus of Mass XVII for the right hand in E major (four sharps), with the Latin words under the notes.
tips: Four sharps: F♯, C♯, G♯ and D♯.
Chant has no strict beat: keep the notes flowing evenly.
lessons.why: a single chant line, but in four sharps
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik
lessons.learn: The opening of Mozart's serenade in G major. Short rests between the notes make it crisp; the second phrase uses F♯.
tips: Lift the hand during the eighth rests.
Play the quarter notes short and bright.
lessons.why: short opening theme with simple chords

lessons.title: Arirang (Korean folk song, easy piano)
lessons.learn: The best-loved Korean folk song, in 3/4 with a gentle left-hand accompaniment and the words under the melody.
tips: One sharp: F♯.
Sing "Arirang, arirang, arariyo" as you play to feel the phrases.
lessons.why: a folk tune with a light accompaniment
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML score

lessons.title: Greensleeves (easy arrangement)
lessons.learn: A longer arrangement of the old English tune in 3/4, with fingering.
tips: Feel the swing of three beats in a bar.
Follow the fingering written in the score.
lessons.why: a slow tune in 3/4 with a simple left hand
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML arrangement from MuseScore.com

lessons.title: Aria in D minor (BWV 515)
lessons.learn: A short, songlike aria from the Anna Magdalena notebook.
tips: Sing the melody in your head as you play it.
Let the bass support without covering the tune.
lessons.syl: Level 2 · Complete list: Aria in D Minor, BWV 515

lessons.title: The First Noel
lessons.learn: The Christmas carol with its words under the melody, in 3/4, with a simple left-hand accompaniment.
tips: Sing the words as you play to feel the phrases.
Count three beats in each bar.
lessons.why: a carol tune with a simple left hand
lessons.license: Public domain music; free MusicXML arrangement from MuseScore.com

lessons.title: Chord progression study
lessons.learn: The famous I–V–vi–IV progression (C, G, A minor, F) with flowing right-hand arpeggios. Hundreds of pop songs use these four chords.
tips: Each right-hand bar uses one chord shape: 1 2 3 5, back down.
Say the chord names as you play: C, G, A minor, F.

lessons.title: Soldier's March, Op. 68 No. 2
lessons.learn: A crisp little march with chords in both hands. A steady beat is everything here.
tips: Play the chords short and bright, exactly together.
March: never rush.
lessons.syl: Level 2 · List B: Soldier's March, op. 68, no. 2 (Schumann)

lessons.title: Ear tests
lessons.learn: Clap back a rhythm, name minor thirds, major thirds and perfect fifths, tell major from minor, and play back a five-note melody.

lessons.title: Sight reading
lessons.learn: Tap a rhythm with rests at sight, then play a four-bar melody shared between the hands that may move beyond the five-finger position.

lessons.title: Two-octave scales hands together: D, F and B♭ major
lessons.learn: From Level 3 the scales are played hands together, an octave apart. Each hand keeps its own fingering, so the thumbs cross at different moments.
tips: Practise each hand alone first, then together slowly with Wait for me.
Watch where each thumb goes: in D major the right thumb plays D and G, the left thumb A and D.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Harmonic minor scales hands together: B, D and G
lessons.learn: B minor has two sharps (F♯, C♯) and raises A to A♯; D minor raises C to C♯; G minor raises F to F♯. In B minor the left hand starts with finger 4.
tips: Left hand in B minor: 4 3 2 1, 4 3 2 1.
In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Melodic minor scales hands together: B, D and G
lessons.learn: Melodic minor, hands together: the 6th and 7th notes are raised going up and natural coming down.
tips: In the exam technique is played from memory: when it feels easy, turn on ⋯ → Hide the notes.

lessons.title: Formula pattern in D major
